prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- For the best combination of price, selection and reliable installation in Pleasanton, most people start with Discount Tire (good nationwide reputation) or one of the national service centers (Firestone/NTB/Pep Boys) for convenience and warranty handling. For more personalized service and attention to detail, a well-reviewed independent Pleasanton shop is often better.  
- If you want, I can look up current top-rated shops in Pleasanton and compare prices/warranties for your vehicle — tell me your car make/model/year and tire size (or let me search for nearby shops).

How to choose where to buy and who does the best installation
1. Decide whether you want a big chain or a local shop
   - Chains (Discount Tire, Firestone, Pep Boys, etc.): predictable pricing, large inventories, standard warranties, usually good install consistency.
   - Independent shops: often better customer service, flexibility on small issues, and careful techs who’ll take time on hub cleaning, torque, and TPMS. Quality varies by shop, so check reviews.

2. Check three things for “best installation”
   - Technician qualifications and equipment: ASE-certified techs, modern balancing/alignment machines.
   - What the install includes: mounting, wheel balancing, new valve stems, TPMS reset/relearn, torque to spec, road-force balancing if needed, and whether they clean hubs and re-torque after a short drive.
   - Warranties and follow-up: lifetime rotation/balancing policies, road-hazard coverage, alignment guarantees.

3. How to evaluate shops quickly
   - Read Google and Yelp recent reviews; focus on installation-specific comments (did they torque/tighten, did they fix vibration, was alignment offered).
   - Ask for an itemized quote over the phone (tires, mount & balance, taxes, disposal fee, alignment).
   - Ask if alignment is included or if they’ll recommend/perform one if you buy tires.
   - Ask about wait time, whether they’ll keep you posted, and what post-install checks they do.

Practical checklist to use when you go
- Bring or know your tire size and VIN. Ask for the exact tire model and load/speed rating.
- Inspect the tires before they leave the counter (correct model, no visible damage).
- After install, ask them to show you the torque spec used and to document lug nut torque.
- Test-drive for vibrations and return promptly if anything feels off.
- Keep the receipt and warranty paperwork.

If you want I’ll:
- Look up the top-rated tire stores and installers in Pleasanton right now and compare prices, or
- Recommend specific tire models (all-season, touring, performance, winter) if you tell me your vehicle, driving style and budget.
